observations: Frame 1 (start): ONE duplicated chromosome rendered as two joined pink sister chromatids centered on the vertical metaphase-plate line; two yellow kinetochores sit at the centromeric region; a horizontal spindle fiber from each blue pole reaches the respective kinetochore, giving correct bipolar (amphitelic) kinetochore-microtubule attachment.

Frame 2 (end): the joined pair has resolved into TWO distinct pink daughter chromatids, each located between the metaphase plate and one pole (poleward of the equator); each retains exactly one yellow kinetochore and one fiber to its own pole, with attachment polarity preserved (left chromatid→left pole, right chromatid→right pole); no extra or duplicated chromatid copies are present.

Spatial landmarks (two blue poles, central vertical metaphase-plate line) are present and consistent across both frames, so the start/end states are mutually coherent as a metaphase→anaphase transition.
Molecular cohesin cleavage is not drawn, matching the schema's excluded-process scope; only the observable breakdown of the sister connection is shown.
limitations: Only two endpoint frames are available; the intermediate trajectory and the actual direction/speed of poleward movement cannot be verified from these alone (positions are consistent with poleward motion but do not prove it).

Chromatid shapes are schematic trapezoids rather than anatomically detailed condensed chromosomes; acceptable for a grades 10–12 schematic but not a structural proof of centromere/kinetochore morphology.
No teaching labels are present in the pixels (expected; labels are added post-generation), so identity of poles/kinetochores/plate is inferred from color and position conventions.
Cohesin degradation and spindle-assembly-checkpoint regulation are out of scope and not depicted; no causal claim about the separation mechanism is made or testable from these frames.
